stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // VAMPIRE

//L3Harris

📍Melbourne, FL

Tech: Precision strike

Platform: Portable C-UxS kit

Goal: Counter drones and remotely piloted platforms in littoral environments.

Why: A self-contained weapons solution combines reconnaissance and precision strike against drones across domains.

Ticker: NYSE: LHX

Traction: Selected by the U.S. Navy to deliver VAMPIRE counter-unmanned systems, per L3Harris. L3Harris is also delivering VAMPIRE systems to the U.S. Army.

The U.S. Navy has selected L3Harris to deliver VAMPIRE counter-unmanned systems, adding to the service's part of a wider integrated counter-drone architecture. The kit is built to mount on most cargo-bed vehicles and fire APKWS or other laser-guided munitions.

L3Harris says it is ruggedizing the system for maritime conditions. The company also notes that its Wraith Shield software and Drone Guardian systems can be paired with VAMPIRE for layered defense against unmanned threats.

Source: L3Harris Technologies, 08SEP26

Image: L3Harris (courtesy)

fields.headline: STATE PICKS PARAVISION FOR UP TO $6.5M
fields.deck: The five-year contract covers digital identity assurance, per federal records.

frames.mediaQuery: Paravision facial recognition deepfake detection identity verification

stories.caption:
The State Department has granted facial recognition developer Paravision an award of up to $6.5 million, according to federal procurement records. The records label the work "digital detection/identity assurance."

The department signed the contract on September 23 and initially committed $1.3 million. It is a fixed-price agreement that can run through September 2031. The department bought it through simplified acquisition procedures as a small-business set-aside, and only one offer was received.

The public records do not name the Paravision products involved. The label lines up with tools Paravision sells to catch manipulated and AI-generated faces, such as its deepfake detection, liveness detection and facial recognition software. The records do not confirm which of those, if any, the award covers.

The September award is much larger than an earlier State Department purchase from Paravision. On April 30 the department placed a $24,717 purchase card order for a software license. Public records do not show whether that order was a test, a pilot or a step toward the larger contract.

Source: Biometric Update, 17 October 2026

Image: Paravision (courtesy)

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // LIGHTFISH

//Seasats

📍San Diego, CA

Tech: Autonomous surveillance

Platform: Unmanned surface vessel

Goal: Provide persistent surveillance to detect illegal maritime activity, including drug trafficking and unauthorized vessel ingress, across the Gulf of America.

Why: Crewed patrols are limited by crew endurance, operating cost and the area one asset can cover at a time.

Backers: Shield Capital, L3Harris Technologies, Konvoy Ventures

Traction: Lightfish vessels deployed on the Gulf of America in support of U.S. maritime border security, per Seasats. Lightfish vessels have operated on the Rio Grande since January 2026.

Seasats said it has deployed a fleet of Lightfish unmanned surface vessels to help U.S. border agencies watch the water. The fleet launched from the Texas coast and will run autonomous surveillance over the Gulf. The work grows out of a Homeland Defense effort that Seasats had already supported on the southern border, including Operation River Wall.

Each Lightfish is roughly 11 feet long and weighs 340 pounds. The solar-powered boats can stay on station for multiple months and can be launched by two people. Sensor payloads swap in and out on a single hull, and the company says its prior missions have used electro-optical and infrared cameras, signals gear and sonar.

Assistant Secretary of War for Homeland Defense and Americas Security Affairs Mark R. Ditlevson said industry partners such as Seasats help the department "close critical capability gaps" and that the Lightfish has been prototyped and piloted on the Rio Grande and in the Gulf of America.

Source: Seasats via PR Newswire, Oct. 2, 2026

Image: U.S. Army photo by Spc. Jacob D. Harrell

The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.

stories.caption:
Three MCU stories from last week, each linked to its original card.

Microchip Technology acquired Austin-based VORAGO Technologies, adding radiation-hardened microcontrollers, microprocessors and its HARDSIL process technology. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Lockheed Martin unveiled PAC-3 Edge for the U.S. Army's Future Interceptor competition. The company says testing is planned for 2027, with deployment targeted by 2031.

The Florida National Guard ran Drone Crucible 26.3 at Camp Blanding, Sept. 26 to Oct. 2. The Guard reported that connected drone data and dedicated technical specialists were both needed to keep the shared picture working.

Source: MilCityUSA, Oct. 2026 (week of Oct. 5 coverage); original sources Microchip Technology, Oct. 9, 2026; Lockheed Martin, Oct. 9, 2026; Florida National Guard, Oct. 6, 2026.
